formulations.label: Film-coated tablets 600 mg calcium / 400 IU vitamin D3
formulations.strengths: 600 mg elemental calcium (as calcium carbonate 1500 mg) + 10 micrograms colecalciferol (400 IU) per tablet
formulations.note: Closest UK match for a 600 mg calcium + vitamin D tablet. The clinic product states 200 IU vitamin D per tablet; this UK tablet has 400 IU.

src.q: Each film-coated tablet contains 600 mg calcium (as calcium carbonate 1500 mg) and 10 micrograms of colecalciferol (equivalent to 400 IU vitamin D3)

formulations.label: Film-coated tablets 750 mg calcium carbonate / 200 IU vitamin D3
formulations.strengths: Calcium carbonate 750 mg (300 mg elemental calcium) + colecalciferol 200 IU (5 micrograms) per tablet
formulations.note: UK product with 200 IU vitamin D per tablet, but only 300 mg elemental calcium per tablet (the usual dose is 2 tablets twice a day).

src.q: Calcium carbonate: 750 mg equivalent to 300 mg of elemental calcium.
Colecalciferol: 200 I.U. equivalent to 5 μg vitamin D3.

items.t: Prevention and treatment of vitamin D and calcium deficiency in the elderly; supplement as an adjunct to specific osteoporosis treatment in patients at risk of deficiency.

src.q: Prevention and treatment of vitamin D and calcium deficiency in the elderly.
Vitamin D and calcium supplement as an adjunct to specific osteoporosis treatments of patients who are at risk of vitamin D and calcium deficiency.

items.t: Adjunct to osteoporosis therapy; supplementation (e.g. in pregnancy, vitamin D dependent osteomalacia); prevention and treatment of calcium/vitamin D deficiency, especially in housebound and institutionalised elderly people.

src.q: As an adjunct to specific therapy for osteoporosis and in situations requiring therapeutic supplementation of malnutrition e.g. in pregnancy and established vitamin D dependent osteomalacia.
The prevention and treatment of calcium deficiency/vitamin D deficiency especially in the housebound and institutionalised elderly subjects.

items.t: Patients already taking thiazide diuretics and/or cardiac glycosides should be referred to their doctor (not suitable for pharmacy supply).

src.q: Patients who are already taking thiazide diuretics and/or cardiac glycosides should be referred to their doctor prior to concomitant use (i.e. not suitable for pharmacy supply).

items.t: Adults and elderly: 1 tablet twice a day (e.g. morning and evening). Consider dose reduction according to calcium monitoring.

src.q: Adults and elderly One tablet twice a day (e.g. one tablet in the morning and one tablet in the evening).
Dose reduction should be considered as necessary following the monitoring of calcium levels

items.t: Adults, elderly and children over 12 years: 2 tablets twice a day (morning and evening).

src.q: Adults and Elderly and children above 12 years of age: Two tablets to be taken twice a day, preferably two tablets each morning and two tablets each evening.

items.t: 600 mg calcium / 400 IU tablet: not intended for children and adolescents.

src.q: Accrete D3 film coated tablets are not intended for use in children and adolescents.

items.t: 300 mg calcium / 200 IU tablet: not recommended under 12 years; over 12 years same dose as adults.

src.q: Children: Not recommended for children under 12 years.

items.t: Hypercalcaemia or hypercalciuria, or conditions causing them (e.g. myeloma, bone metastases, other malignant bone disease, sarcoidosis); primary hyperparathyroidism.

src.q: Diseases and/or conditions resulting in hypercalcaemia and/or hypercalciuria (e.g. myeloma, bone metastases or other malignant bone disease, sarcoidosis; primary hyperparathyroidism).
Absolute contra-indications are hypercalcaemia resulting for example from myeloma, bone metastases or other malignant bone disease, sarcoidosis, primary hyperparathyroidism and vitamin D overdosage.

src.q: Hypervitaminosis D
primary hyperparathyroidism and vitamin D overdosage

src.q: Severe renal impairment and renal failure
Severe renal failure.

items.t: 600 mg calcium / 400 IU tablet: nephrolithiasis / nephrocalcinosis.

src.q: Nephrolithiasis / nephrocalcinosis

items.t: Hypersensitivity to the active substances or excipients; the 600 mg / 400 IU tablet SmPC names soya or peanut allergy.

src.q: Hypersensitivity to the active substances or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1 (including soya or peanut).
Hypersensitivity to any of the tablet ingredients.

items.t: Relative contraindications (both SmPCs): osteoporosis due to prolonged immobilisation, renal stones, severe hypercalciuria.

src.q: Relative contra-indications are osteoporosis due to prolonged immobilisation, renal stones, severe hypercalciuria.
Relative contra-indications are osteoporosis due to prolonged immobilisation, renal stones, severe hypercalciuria.

items.t: Long-term treatment: monitor serum calcium and renal function (serum creatinine), especially in elderly patients on cardiac glycosides or diuretics and in stone formers. Reduce or stop if hypercalcaemia or impaired renal function; reduce or interrupt if urinary calcium exceeds 7.5 mmol/24 h (300 mg/24 h).

src.q: During long-term treatment, serum calcium levels should be followed and renal function should be monitored through measurements of serum creatinine.
In case of hypercalcaemia or signs of impaired renal function the dose should be reduced or the treatment discontinued.
It is advisable to reduce or interrupt treatment temporarily if urinary calcium exceeds 7.5 mmol/24 h (300 mg/24 h).

items.t: Mild to moderate renal failure or mild hypercalciuria: supervise carefully with periodic plasma calcium and urinary calcium checks. History of renal stones: measure urinary calcium to exclude hypercalciuria.

src.q: Patients with mild to moderate renal failure or mild hypercalciuria should be supervised carefully including periodic checks of plasma calcium levels and urinary calcium excretion.
In patients with a history of renal stones, urinary calcium excretion should be measured to exclude hypercalciuria.

items.t: Sarcoidosis: prescribe with caution (increased activation of vitamin D); monitor serum and urine calcium.

src.q: should be prescribed with caution to patients suffering from sarcoidosis, due to the risk of increased metabolism of vitamin D into its active form.

items.t: Immobilised patients with osteoporosis: use with caution (increased risk of hypercalcaemia).

src.q: should be used with caution in immobilised patients with osteoporosis due to increased risk of hypercalcaemia.

items.t: Allow for calcium and vitamin D from other sources. Extra calcium or vitamin D only under close medical supervision with frequent serum and urine calcium checks. Large amounts of calcium with absorbable alkali can cause milk-alkali syndrome (hypercalcaemia, alkalosis, renal impairment).

src.q: Additional doses of calcium or vitamin D should be taken under close medical supervision.
Milk-alkali syndrome (Burnett's syndrome), i.e. hypercalcaemia, alkalosis and renal impairment can develop when large amounts of calcium are ingested with absorbable alkali.

items.t: Contains sucrose: people with hereditary fructose intolerance, glucose-galactose malabsorption or sucrase-isomaltase insufficiency should not take it.

src.q: Patients with rare hereditary problems of fructose intolerance, glucose-galactose malabsorption or sucrase-isomaltase insufficiency should not take this medicine.

items.t: Thiazides reduce urinary calcium excretion: risk of hypercalcaemia. The 600 mg / 400 IU tablet SmPC says monitor serum calcium regularly.

src.q: Due to increased risk of hypercalcaemia, serum calcium should be regularly monitored during concomitant use of thiazide diuretics.
The risk of hypercalcaemia should be considered in patients taking thiazide diuretics

items.tag: Separation times (they differ between UK sources)
items.t: 600 mg / 400 IU tablet SmPC: tetracyclines at least 2 hours before or 4-6 hours after calcium; quinolones 2 hours before or 6 hours after; iron and thyroid hormones at least 2 hours apart. 300 mg / 200 IU tablet SmPC: allow at least 4 hours before taking the calcium after thyroxine, quinolones, tetracyclines or iron.

src.q: tetracycline preparations should be administered at least two hours before or four to six hours after oral intake of calcium.
Quinolone antibiotics should be taken two hours before or six hours after intake of calcium.
the iron, zinc or strontium preparation should be taken at a distance of two hours from the calcium preparation.
It is recommended that taking Accrete D3 film-coated tablets be spaced at least 2 hours from these medicines.

Calcium salts may reduce the absorption of thyroxine, bisphosphonates, sodium fluoride, quinolone or tetracycline antibiotics, zinc, strontium ranelate and iron. It is advisable to allow a minimum period of four hours before taking calcium.

items.t: Levothyroxine SmPC: calcium salts may reduce levothyroxine absorption; separate by 4-5 hours.

src.q: Absorption of levothyroxine (thyroxine) possibly reduced by antacids, calcium salts
(administration should be separated by 4-5 hours)

items.t: Ciprofloxacin SmPC: give ciprofloxacin 1-2 hours before or at least 4 hours after calcium-containing products.

src.q: multivalent cation-containing drugs and mineral supplements (e.g. calcium, magnesium, aluminium, iron)
ciprofloxacin should be administered either 1-2 hours before or at least 4 hours after these preparations

items.t: Hypercalcaemia may increase cardiac glycoside toxicity: monitor ECG and serum calcium.

src.q: Hypercalcaemia may increase the toxicity of cardiac glycosides during treatment with calcium and vitamin D. Patients should be monitored with regard to electrocardiogram (ECG) and serum calcium levels.

items.t: Systemic corticosteroids reduce calcium absorption; the dose may need to be increased.

src.q: Systemic corticosteroids reduce calcium absorption. During concomitant use, it may be necessary to increase the dose of Accrete D3 film-coated tablets.

items.t: Bisphosphonates or sodium fluoride at least 3 hours before the calcium tablet. Rifampicin, phenytoin and barbiturates may reduce vitamin D activity. Colestyramine and paraffin oil may reduce vitamin D absorption.

src.q: these medicinal products should be administered at least three hours before the intake of Accrete D3 film-coated tablet since gastrointestinal absorption may be reduced.
Rifampicin, phenytoin or barbiturates may reduce the activity of vitamin D3, since they increase the rate of its metabolism.

items.t: Do not take within 2 hours of foods high in oxalic acid (spinach, sorrel, rhubarb) or phytic acid (whole cereals).

src.q: The patient should not take calcium products within two hours of eating foods high in oxalic acid and phytic acid.

items.t: Contraindicated in severe renal impairment and renal failure (no eGFR/CrCl threshold given). In severe renal insufficiency colecalciferol is not metabolised normally; other forms of vitamin D should be used.

src.q: Accrete D3 film-coated tablets should not be used in patients with severe renal impairment.
In patients with severe renal insufficiency, vitamin D in the form of colecalciferol is not metabolised normally and other forms of vitamin D should be used

items.t: Renal impairment: use vitamin D with caution and monitor calcium and phosphate; risk of soft tissue calcification, hyperphosphataemia, nephrolithiasis and nephrocalcinosis.

src.q: Vitamin D should be used with caution in patients with impairment of renal function and the effect on calcium and phosphate levels should be monitored.
Patients with renal impairment: potential risk of hyperphosphatemia, nephrolithiasis and nephrocalcinosis.

items.t: 600 mg / 400 IU tablet: no dose adjustment in hepatic impairment. The 300 mg / 200 IU tablet SmPC gives no hepatic advice.

src.q: Hepatic impairment No dose adjustment is required.

items.t: May be used for calcium and vitamin D deficiency. In pregnancy the daily dose should not exceed 1500 mg calcium and 600 IU vitamin D; avoid any overdose (prolonged hypercalcaemia can harm the child).

src.q: Accrete D3 film-coated tablets may be given during pregnancy in cases of calcium and vitamin D3 deficiency. During pregnancy the daily dose should not exceed 1500 mg of calcium and 600 IU of vitamin D.
In pregnant women, all calcium or vitamin D overdoses must be avoided

items.t: Use in pregnancy only under the direction of a physician; allow for calcium and vitamin D from other sources. Take iron supplements at a different time.

src.q: During pregnancy and lactation, treatment with Adcal-D3 Caplets should always be under the direction of a physician.
If the patient requires administration of both Adcal-D3 Caplets and iron supplements, they should be taken at different times

items.t: Can be used during breastfeeding. Calcium and vitamin D pass into breast milk: consider this when giving the infant extra vitamin D.

src.q: Accrete D3 film-coated tablets can be used during breast-feeding. Calcium and vitamin D pass into breast milk. This should be considered when giving additional vitamin D to the child.

items.t: Use during lactation under the direction of a physician.

src.q: During pregnancy and lactation, treatment with Adcal-D3 Caplets should always be under the direction of a physician.

items.t: No known harmful effect of normal calcium and vitamin D levels on fertility; no product data.

src.q: There is no known harmful effect of endogenous levels of calcium and vitamin D in the normal range on fertility.

items.t: No common effects listed. Uncommon: hypercalcaemia, hypercalciuria. Rare: constipation, flatulence, nausea, abdominal pain, diarrhoea; pruritus, rash, urticaria.

src.q: Uncommon: Hypercalcaemia and hypercalciuria.
Rare: Constipation, flatulence, nausea, abdominal pain, and diarrhoea.

items.t: Hypersensitivity reactions (pruritus, wheezing, urticaria, oropharyngeal swelling, angioedema) have been reported.

src.q: Hypersensitivity reactions including pruritus, wheezing, urticaria, oropharyngeal swelling and angioedema have been reported in the post-marketing environment.

items.t: Overdose: hypercalcaemia (anorexia, thirst, nausea, vomiting, constipation, polyuria, confusion; severe cases arrhythmias, coma). Milk-alkali syndrome. Stop calcium and vitamin D (and thiazides, cardiac glycosides), rehydrate.

src.q: Extreme hypercalcaemia may result in coma and death.
The treatment with calcium and vitamin D must be discontinued. Treatment with thiazide diuretics, lithium, vitamin A, vitamin D and cardiac glycosides must also be discontinued.

items.t: History of renal stones: measure urinary calcium to exclude hypercalciuria.

src.q: In patients with a history of renal stones, urinary calcium excretion should be measured to exclude hypercalciuria.

items.t: Long-term treatment: serum calcium and renal function (serum creatinine); urinary calcium.

src.q: During long-term treatment, serum calcium levels should be followed and renal function should be monitored through measurements of serum creatinine.
With long-term treatment it is advisable to monitor serum and urinary calcium levels and kidney function

items.t: Reduce or stop temporarily if urinary calcium exceeds 7.5 mmol/24 hours (300 mg/24 hours); reduce or stop if hypercalcaemia or impaired renal function.

src.q: reduce or stop treatment temporarily if urinary calcium exceeds 7.5 mmol/24 hours (300 mg/24 hours)
In case of hypercalcaemia or signs of impaired renal function the dose should be reduced or the treatment discontinued.

items.t: 600 mg / 400 IU tablet: swallow with a glass of water or juice within one and a half hours of a meal, without chewing; may be broken in half to help swallowing.

src.q: It is recommended that the film-coated tablet is taken within one and a half hours of a meal with a glass of water or juice, without chewing it. The tablet can be broken in half, if needed.

items.t: Keep a gap between this tablet and levothyroxine, quinolone or tetracycline antibiotics, and iron (2-6 hours depending on the medicine and the SmPC).

src.q: Quinolone antibiotics should be taken two hours before or six hours after intake of calcium.

src.q: Allowances should be made for calcium and vitamin D supplements from other sources.
